channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: How Air Traffic Control Radar Actually Tracks Planes
item.description: Controllers watching busy airspace do more than bounce radio waves off metal. Modern tracking blends radar with planes broadcasting their own exact position automatically.

item.title: How Airlines Actually Decide Boarding Groups
item.description: Boarding order looks arbitrary from the gate, but airlines run simulations balancing loyalty tiers, fare class, seat location, and aisle-clogging physics before calling groups.

item.title: How Airport Duty-Free Shops Actually Make Money
item.description: Duty-free prices look like a discount, but the real profit engine is rent-paying concession deals, a captive audience with time to kill, and margins high-street shops never charge.

item.title: How Airport Immigration E-Gates Actually Verify Your Identity
item.description: E-gates at Dubai and Riyadh airports clear travelers in seconds. Behind that speed sits a chain of passport chip reads, live face scans, and watchlist checks running invisibly.

item.title: How Airport Lounges Actually Decide Who Gets In
item.description: A lounge entry system juggles airline status tiers, credit card deals, day-pass sales, and a hard seat limit, all decided by an agent scanning your card in under ten seconds.

item.title: How Arabic Calligraphy Gets Digitized for Computers
item.description: Arabic script joins letters into flowing shapes that change with every neighbor. Turning that into a working computer font took decades of type engineering most readers never see.

item.title: How Camel Milk Is Actually Processed and Sold in the Gulf
item.description: Camel milk cannot be pasteurized on the same equipment as cow milk. Getting it into supermarket cartons and chocolate bars required rebuilding the dairy process from scratch.

item.title: How Cinema Projection Changed From Film to Digital
item.description: A movie reel weighing dozens of kilograms and a hard drive weighing a few hundred grams can show the exact same film. That transition reshaped how movies are shipped worldwide.

item.title: How CPAP Machines Actually Treat Sleep Apnea
item.description: A CPAP machine does not force air into the lungs. It uses gentle, continuous pressure to prop open an airway that would otherwise collapse dozens of times a night.

item.title: How Desert Hot Air Balloon Rides Actually Work
item.description: Every sunrise balloon flight over the Dubai desert depends on a narrow weather window, a burner strong enough to lift a basket, and pilots reading wind layers guests never notice.

item.title: How Desert Mirages Actually Form
item.description: That shimmering pool of water on a hot highway is not an illusion your eyes invent. It is light bending through layers of unevenly heated air, and it can be photographed.

item.title: How E Ink Displays Actually Work
item.description: E-ink screens on e-readers can hold an image for weeks without power. The trick is millions of microscopic capsules filled with charged black and white particles.

item.title: How Falcon Hospitals in the UAE Actually Treat Birds
item.description: Falcons in the Gulf carry passports and get CT scans. Behind that sits a genuinely sophisticated avian medical system built around a bird woven deep into Emirati heritage.

item.title: How Food Delivery Apps Actually Price Your Order
item.description: The total on a delivery app is never just the menu price. Commission fees, dynamic delivery pricing, and small markups on the food itself all stack quietly before checkout.

item.title: How Frankincense and Myrrh Are Actually Harvested and Traded
item.description: Long before oil, the Arabian Peninsula grew rich on tree resin. The ancient harvesting method has barely changed, but the global trade around it has been transformed completely.

item.title: How Honeybee Colonies Actually Make Honey
item.description: Honey is not simply stored nectar. It is nectar transformed twice, once by enzymes inside a bee and once by evaporation in the hive, into a substance that can last millennia.

item.title: How Marathon Course Certification Actually Works
item.description: A marathon world record can be wiped from the books if the course measured a few meters short. Behind every certified race sits a surprisingly rigorous bicycle measurement science.

item.title: How the Jebel Jais Zipline Actually Works
item.description: Riders on the world’s longest zipline hit highway speeds thousands of feet above a desert canyon. The system holding them up relies on physics most guests never think to ask about.

item.title: How the Ramadan Cannon-Firing Tradition Actually Works
item.description: A cannon blast tells millions of fasting people it is time to eat. Behind that boom sits a centuries-old Egyptian tradition and a modern logistics operation across many cities.

item.title: How Zamzam Water Is Actually Bottled and Distributed Worldwide
item.description: Millions of pilgrims want to bring Zamzam water home every year. Saudi authorities built an entire logistics and quality-control system to move a sacred well’s output worldwide.
